requirement: sorted() returns a list where every element is less than or equal to the next element.
driftDescription: Uses strict less-than (<) instead of less-than-or-equal (<=), misses equal elements

requirement: sorted() returns a permutation of its input: every element in the input appears in the output the same number of times.
driftDescription: Only checks that length is preserved, not that the multiset of elements is preserved

requirement: sorted() is stable: elements that compare equal appear in the same relative order in the output as in the input.
driftDescription: Only checks that the output is sorted by key, does not verify relative order is preserved for equal elements

requirement: str.split() with no arguments splits on runs of whitespace, discards leading and trailing whitespace, and returns no empty strings.
driftDescription: Only checks that result is non-empty for non-empty input; misses the no-empty-strings guarantee and leading/trailing whitespace handling

requirement: str.split(sep) splits the string at every occurrence of sep and the pieces joined back with sep reconstruct the original string.
driftDescription: Only checks count of pieces equals occurrences+1, does not verify that joining pieces reconstructs the original

requirement: list.index(x) returns the index of the first occurrence of x in the list, and raises ValueError if x is not present.
driftDescription: Only checks the happy path (element present); does not check that ValueError is raised when element is absent

requirement: set.union() returns a set containing every element that appears in at least one of the input sets.
driftDescription: Only checks that the result is a superset of the first set; does not check the second set's elements are included

requirement: set.intersection() returns a set containing exactly those elements that appear in all of the input sets.
driftDescription: Only checks that result is a subset of the first set; misses that result must also be a subset of the second set and must contain all common elements

requirement: set.difference(other) returns a set containing elements that are in the first set but not in the other set.
driftDescription: Checks that no element in result appears in b, but does not check that all elements of a not in b are included (subset direction missing)

requirement: reversed() returns an iterator whose elements are the elements of the input sequence in reverse order.
driftDescription: Only checks that the reversed list has the same length as the original; does not check order is actually reversed
